summary: Confirmed DONE. 60633eff3 replaced the single scan-cache.json with 64 hash-keyed shard files. Shards are versioned per change, only dirty shards are rewritten (atomically, with yields between them, debounced 1 s off the request path), the legacy file is migrated once, and the cache is unloaded after 10 idle minutes. e5e676f95 shrank what is stored: per-file 15-minute slots, with keyed rows only for responses that carry a dedupe key (16-hex key plus 7 numbers). The 0.3-0.6 s single parse, the full rewrite per open and the ~500k-record oversized cliff are all gone. The SQLite proposal was not taken, but the finding's own 'shard the JSON per file' alternative is implemented, along with per-file aggregates. I found no other callers, missing persistence paths, locking races or test gaps. Lock ordering is persistLock -> loadLock with no inversion, persist snapshots synchronously, and a failed write stays dirty. Two minor residuals sit next to the fix; neither reopens the finding.

evidence.note: 64 shards, chosen from the first byte of the SHA-256 file key. Every cache key, including OpenCode's (opencodeUsageReader.ts:215,222,361), comes from usageCacheFileKey, so keys spread evenly.
TrackedUsageScanCache bumps a per-shard version on set/delete/clear. restore() and unload() do not dirty anything.

persist() captures dirtyShards() and partitions entries in one synchronous step. It rewrites only dirty shards, removes empty ones, yields between shards and marks a shard persisted only after its write succeeds. A concurrent mutation bumps the version, so that shard stays dirty.

load() reads 64 small shards with concurrency 8 and decodes each one right after its read. Legacy migration runs only when no shard exists. An oversized legacy file is left on the first load and removed after a later load (exists check at 157-163).
persistLock serializes the debounced background persist, the shutdown finalizer and unload, so two persists never write the same shard at once.
The idle watcher persists, then unloads under scanSemaphore -> persistLock -> loadLock. ensureLoaded takes only loadLock, so the locks cannot deadlock.
An unchanged file is reused without set(), so nothing is dirtied. Only a re-parsed file dirties its own shard.

The v6 serialized form holds per-file slots plus compact keyed rows. Codex (dedupeKey null, codexTranscript.ts:140) folds fully into slots. The commit reports 41.5 MB -> 2.4 MB (Claude) and 41.9 MB -> 0.9 MB (Codex).

Tests cover migration, rewriting only the changed shard, unload/reload, removing a shard whose last entry is deleted, retention on load, a shared concurrent load and cleanup of a leftover legacy file.

Residual: capUsageScanCache still weighs entries by aggregate.recordCount. That made sense when it was added in 60633eff3 (entry.records.length), but after e5e676f95 memory scales with keys.length + slots.length. Fully folded Codex/keyless files count as if each response were resident.

Every summary runs the cap. A user above 1M resident responses has the oldest files evicted after each summary. Those files are re-parsed on the next request under the per-source budget (UsageService.ts:97-99, 830-838: 100k records / 5 s), so 'All'/'90d' can keep reporting transcript-scan-budget and dirty those shards each time. Rare heavy-user case.

Residual: on load, the 120-day retention is applied unconditionally, while all-time summaries use cutoff 0 (UsageService.ts:1082-1083). In practice this is masked: the default 30d view (apps/web/src/components/settings/StatisticsPanel.tsx:57) already prunes the same files, as the old code did at f1be4abc7.

fixDefects:
No defect reopens the finding. Minor residuals:
1. capUsageScanCache (usageScanCache.ts:509-522), called at UsageService.ts:1085 and usageScanCacheStore.ts:181, still counts recordCount against USAGE_SCAN_CACHE_RECORD_LIMIT = 1,000,000. After e5e676f95 the resident cost is keys + slots. The cap therefore over-evicts folded (Codex/keyless) files for no memory gain. Above the limit it evicts the oldest files at the end of every summary. Those files are re-parsed next time under the 100k-record / 5 s per-source budget, and coverage may never converge for 'All'. In the old code, the in-memory cache converged within a process lifetime.
2. The load-time retention prune (usageScanCacheStore.ts:173-180) evicts files older than 120 days even when the request is all-time (cutoff 0). This is masked because the default 30d view prunes them anyway. It is pre-existing retention policy, not part of the monolith cost.
3. The first usage open after startup or after an idle unload still decodes all 64 shards eagerly. That is now tens of ms, not a stall.
implementationSketch: Optional, low value: in apps/server/src/usage/usageScanCache.ts capUsageScanCache, weigh each entry by retained rows (entry.aggregate.keys.length + entry.aggregate.slots.length) instead of aggregate.recordCount. Rename the constant in usageScanCacheStore.ts (e.g. USAGE_SCAN_CACHE_RETAINED_ROW_LIMIT, keep ~1M) and update the callers at UsageService.ts:1085 and usageScanCacheStore.ts:181. Keep MAX_RECORDS_PER_FILE on recordCount for decode validation. Consider weighing SOURCE_CACHED_RECORDS (UsageService.ts:101, 823) the same way, since summary cost is now O(slots + keys). Tests in usageScanCache.test.ts: a Codex-only cache of >1M responses folded into a few thousand slots is not evicted; a Claude keyed cache above the limit still evicts the oldest-mtime files first. Optionally make the load-time retention prune respect all-time usage, either by deferring retention to the summary prune or by keeping it and documenting it as a memory bound.
